readme_snippet: Retry amplification and metastable failure The multiplication Retries compose multiplicatively down a call chain: The amplification arrives exactly when the database is least able to serve it. A dependency 20% degraded now receives 27x traffic. This is the standard route from a blip to an outage. Metastable failure A system is in a metastable failure state when it stays down after the original trigger is gone, because the failure now sustains itself. The defining property: removing the cause does not fix it. Restarting does not fix it, because the retry backlog hits the fresh instance immediately. Teams lose hours restarting things during metastable failures. The only exit is reducing load: block traffic at the edge, let the system drain and stabilize, then ramp back slowly. Put this in the runbook, since knowing it in advance turns a four-hour outage into a fifteen-minute one.
